team_news: As of Fri 9 Oct (Arteta presser) and Thu 8 Oct (Farke presser). Arsenal: OUT William Saliba (back problem from the World Cup; reports range from late October to December, Arteta gives no timeline) and Christos Tzolis (muscle, 'going to be out for a few weeks'). DOUBTS Kai Havertz (muscular/hamstring, sent back early by Germany) and Ezri Konsa (dead leg, withdrew from England): 'Max is available, Ezri and Kai we will see tomorrow.' AVAILABLE Declan Rice (skipped England for load management; reported 'fine and ready', Arteta: 'We have to manage him because he's had a few issues since he came back from the World Cup'), Max Dowman, Ben White, Cristhian Mosquera and Piero Hincapie. No suspensions. Leeds: OUT Daniel James (back, from Wales duty; bench player this season) and Joe Rodon (hamstring, 'it will be a bit until he is back in team training'); Mateo Joseph also listed out in one preview. DOUBTS Jean-Matteo Bahoya (ankle, France U21; back on the pitch Thursday, 'looks better, is a chance') and Harry Wilson (team training since Tuesday; 'We have to wait right now how his body reacts, but there is also a chance for him to be available'). No suspensions. Farke expected to keep a largely unchanged XI from the 0-0 with Palace (speculative, not confirmed).
form_notes: Arsenal are 2nd (W4 L1, GF8 GA4): W3-0 Coventry, W1-0 at Villa, W2-1 Chelsea, W2-0 at Sunderland, then L0-3 at Brighton in the last game before the break. Leeds are 5th and unbeaten (W2 D3, GF7 GA3): W1-0 at Forest, D1-1 Brentford, D1-1 at Brighton, W4-1 Newcastle, D0-0 Palace. Leeds have conceded only 3 goals, which is joint 2nd best in the league. Arsenal's games average 2.4 goals.
xg_notes: Arsenal xG for is about 8.5-9.0 over 5 games (sources vary; one has 6.8), and one source ranks them the best defence on xGA (4.59). Leeds xG for is about 7.2-7.7 (10th on Squawka's xG table). No reliable Leeds xGA found. H2H context only: Arsenal won both 2025-26 meetings, and Arteta is 4/4 in league games against Farke.
pundits: Chris Sutton (BBC): Arsenal 2-0, though one report says he floated 1-1 or 2-2 because of the international-break disruption. Squawka model: 1-0. PredictZ: 3-1. Betfanatics: 2-1. FiFPlay: 2-0. Jones Knows: not found.
reasoning: Opta (68.9%) and the market (about 69% after removing the margin) make Arsenal clear favourites, and their home defensive record plus elite xGA supports a home win. I shade that down to 61% for three reasons: Saliba is reported out, Arsenal were heavily beaten 0-3 at Brighton before the break, and Rice and Havertz were managed or doubtful over the international window. Leeds are unbeaten, have conceded 3 in 5 and have drawn 3 times, so a low-event game is more likely than a rout. With Arsenal at about 1.6-1.7 expected goals and Leeds at about 0.7, a Poisson model makes 1-0 the modal Arsenal-win score, just ahead of 2-0.
risks: If Arsenal score early, Leeds have to open up and the over/2-0+ scores come in. Leeds' set-piece threat and the post-break disruption could still produce a 1-1.
news_update_2026_10_10: Arteta's Friday press conference largely confirmed the earlier picture. Saliba remains out (back, no return date) and Tzolis is out for a few weeks, while Havertz and Konsa are genuine late fitness tests ('we will see tomorrow'). The main change is Declan Rice: previously Arteta only 'hoped' he would be available, but Friday's coverage has him fine and expected to start, albeit with his load managed. White, Mosquera, Hincapie and Dowman are all available. For Leeds, Farke confirmed James and Rodon are out, but James is a bench player and Rodon was already absent; Bahoya and Wilson are now realistic options, a small plus for Leeds' depth. Prices have not moved (Arsenal about 1.40). Rice being available is a modest boost for a midfield starter, so I nudge Arsenal up one point (0.61 to 0.62) and Leeds down one (0.16 to 0.15), leaving the draw at 0.23. I stay below Opta and the market because Saliba is out and Havertz is uncertain. 1-0 remains the modal score.

form_notes: Sunderland are 14th (W1 D1 L3, GF6 GA10): L1-2 at Ipswich, W1-0 Fulham, D1-1 at Brentford, L0-2 Arsenal, L3-5 at Man City. Brighton are 3rd (W3 D1 L1, GF16 GA5): W4-0 Villa, L3-4 at Chelsea, D1-1 at Leeds, W5-0 at Coventry, W3-0 Arsenal. Brighton's away record is W1 D1 L1.

pundits: Chris Sutton (BBC): 1-1. Squawka model: 0-1. Dimers model: 1-1 as the most likely score (12.1%). Statz: 1-1. Last Word on Football: 3-2. BetFanatics: 1-3. Livescore: Brighton to grind out a win.
reasoning: Opta (41.3%), the market (about 42% after removing the margin) and Dimers (39%) all make Brighton the narrow favourites, and their 16 goals and top xG back that up. I trim Brighton and lift the draw because Brighton's attack is depleted: Mitoma, Minteh, Tzimas and Ferguson are out, and Wieffer is out in midfield. Sunderland's xG (9.2 for, 7.4 against) suggests their poor results flatter Brighton's edge. The season's 32% draw rate also points to a tighter game than the 1X2 suggests. Brighton remain my single most likely result, so the primary pick is a one-goal away win (1-2), with BTTS supported by both sides' chance creation. 1-1 is nearly as likely and is my strongest draw candidate if the panel wants more draws.
risks: This is essentially a three-way coin flip. 1-1 is probably the single most likely scoreline, and a Sunderland home win at 30% is very live given their underlying numbers.
news_update_2026_10_10: The press conferences mostly confirmed what was already priced in: Brobbey and Ballard are out for Sunderland, and Mitoma, Minteh, Wieffer, Ferguson and Tzimas are out for Brighton. Three things changed. Diarra, previously described as back in training, is now confirmed out by Le Bris, and Mundle is also out, which thins Sunderland's midfield and wide options. Against that, Reinildo is available, having already served his ban at Man City, so the earlier suspension report was wrong. Brighton get Dunk and Ayari back, although Dunk may be managed. The odds have not moved. The net effect is a small tilt towards Brighton: Sunderland 0.30 to 0.29, Brighton 0.39 to 0.40, draw unchanged at 0.31. None of these players is a first-choice goalkeeper or main striker, so the move stays at one point. 1-2 remains the primary pick, with 1-1 close behind.

news_update_2026_10_10: This is the material change of the three fixtures. The previous entry had Palmer, Joao Pedro, James and Caicedo all doubtful, with one report saying Palmer and Pedro would miss. Alonso's Friday press conference declared all four available ('ready to go'), with only Gittens ruled out. Palmer (playmaker) and Joao Pedro (main striker) are key starters, and Caicedo and James strengthen a side that has conceded 12 in 5, so I move Chelsea up four points (0.48 to 0.52), taking two from the draw (0.27 to 0.25) and two from Bournemouth (0.25 to 0.23). I do not go further because Caicedo has 14 league minutes this season, Palmer is being managed after struggling against Brentford, and the pre-news prices (about 58% Chelsea) may already have assumed most of them would play. Bournemouth's news is unchanged (Scott out four to five weeks, Kluivert out). I remain slightly above Opta (51.8%) and below the market. 2-1 stays the primary score; 1-1 and 2-2 remain the alternatives.
